linus: ran an overnight harness sweep of the hybrid-attn kernels across H100/A100/L40S. quick summary: A100 and L40S look fine, H100 latencies spike at long seqs (>=8192) with batch 8. anyone seen this pattern before?

anita: ugh, saw something similar last month but for tiled-fusion on H100. was that with KV caching enabled?

linus: yep KV cache on. config: `--kv-mode=segmented --prefetch=on --batching=dynamic`

mike: can you paste the exact run command + model shape?

linus: sure: ```bash
./kernel_harness --model gptx-2b --gpus H100,A100,L40S --seq-lens 512,2048,4096,8192,16384 --bs 1,4,8 --iters 100 --kv-mode segmented --tile 64
```

zoe: any perf counters? SM util / L2?

linus: profiler snippet from H100 at seq=8192 bsz=8: ```
SM util: 42% -> should be ~80%
L2 read BW: 1.8 TB/s (spike vs baseline 0.6)
memcpy H2D time (per iter): 3.2ms (baseline 0.3ms)
kernel time 'attn_segmented_fuse': 12.4ms (vs 5.1ms on A100)
```

anita: memcpy spike is a red flag. maybe we hit a fallback path that copies KV pages back and forth? can you dump NVTX ranges or logs that show page churn?

linus: NVTX shows frequent page invalidations around the evict window. also saw console log: `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD_TRIGGERED` ~ every 3 iters.

mike: what about the tiling / tile size? H100 has different cache behavior for tile=64 vs 128. try tile=128 and `--prefetch=off` to see if it stabilizes.

linus: retested quickly with tile=128 + prefetch=off. latency halved, SM util back to ~76%, but quality of attention outputs unchanged (sanity check passed). so prefetch path + segmented KV seems to be the culprit.

zoe: interesting — on A100 that prefetch path improved perf for long seqs. might be a micro-architecture mismatch. can we capture SASS counters / perfAsm for the fused kernel to see if a particular instruction sequence thrashes L2?

linus: grabbed perfAsm diff between H100 slow run and A100 baseline. main divergence is an extra prefetch loop and conditional store sequence that causes many L2 writebacks on H100. attaching a tiny snippet: ```asm
// H100 slow path
LOOP_PREFETCH:
  LDG.E R2, [KV_PAGE_PTR+offset]
  STG.E R3, [TEMP_BUF+idx]   // many stores
  CBNZ R4, LOOP_PREFETCH
```

mike: that store-heavy sequence would explain the L2 spike and memcpy effects. H100's L2 capacity/eviction policy seems to interact badly with our prefetch writes.

anita: proposal: add a micro-optimization toggle that switches prefetch from write-through to read-only prefetch on H100 (and on heuristics: seq>=4096 && bs>=4). Add a metric to the harness to report 'kv_page_writebacks' so we can quantify.

linus: I'm on it. will push a branch with `--kv-prefetch-mode=read` and a small counter exposed by perf-bot. can we schedule another sweep overnight?

perf-bot: queued job: kernel-harness/sweep/1745552222-rerun with flags `--kv-prefetch-mode=read --tile=128` on H100,A100,L40S (ETA 12h) :white_check_mark:

zoe: thanks! also add a quick A/B stable-run check: compare token-seq output hashes to ensure no silent correctness regressions.

linus: will include hash compare. will post results here tomorrow morning. :coffee:
